Iowa broke its midterm voter turnout record, with preliminary reports showing more than 1.38 million ballots cast, representing 63.4% of registered voters. The statewide constitutional amendment received slightly less participation, with turnout of 56%. While statewide races receive much of the attention, voters also decided important local issues. Two counties voted on the size of their boards of supervisors, nearly 50 bond proposals appeared on local ballots, and communities considered questions involving township governance, library boards, emergency medical services (EMS) taxes, local option sales taxes, and hotel and motel taxes.

The post Iowa’s November Election Highlights the Importance of Voter Turnout on Local Issues appeared first on ITR Foundation.
